description: Together, we aim to turn ideas into innovation and make a difference through science and technology.
summary: This project explores the fascinating world of shooting stars, also known as meteors. It explains how meteors are formed when small pieces of space rock enter Earth's atmosphere. The project introduces meteor showers and how they occur when Earth passes through trails of dust left by comets. It also explains why meteors glow brightly and create beautiful streaks of light across the night sky. Through this project, students can learn more about space and develop a greater interest in astronomy.
details: Meteoroids are small pieces of rock or dust that travel through space. When they enter Earth's atmosphere at high speed, they become meteors and produce bright streaks of light. These beautiful lights are commonly known as shooting stars, although they are not real stars. A meteor shower happens when Earth passes through trails of debris left behind by comets or, sometimes, asteroids. By studying meteors, we can understand more about our solar system and the amazing wonders of space.
